描述_ZN: The "Qing Tuo Sui Shoushan Qiyan Daoist Temple Relic Tablet Book", carved in 604, with ink topography, 26 and a half pages cut and mounted. Each opening is 32 cm in length and 35 cm in width. Donated by Mr. Ma Heng.　　This stele is inscribed in seal script with the title "The Stele of the Relic Pagoda at Quyan Dojo, Shushan, Hedong County, Shanxi Province", erected in Yongji County, Shanxi Province. The inscription records that Emperor Wen of the Sui Dynasty ordered the whole country to build the pagoda by "distributing relics in eighty states", and was written by He Deren of Huiji. The regular script is very stable and rigorous, which is a pioneer of the Tang script. The material is covered with sand grains like fish roe, so it is commonly known as "Fish Roe Tablet". The top two dots of the word "monk" in "Gao Xing Ming Monk" still exist. On the back of the booklet, there is a postscript by Mr. Ma Heng on September 6, 1911, verifying that the stele was erected in December of the fourth year of Renshou of the Sui Dynasty (604), revising the error of "the second year of Renshou" in the Qing dynasty's Sun Xingyan's "Huanyu Visiting Monuments". The seal of the collection is inscribed as "Fanshuizhai Zangbi" and "Ma Hengshuping reads the stele".
